records.description:
CHG-20261030-04. Built the missing instrument: a read-only check that answers 'will each workflow actually do its job when it fires?' A workflow pointing at a deleted backend function stays listed as active, keeps a valid trigger, and fails silently at its next fire with nothing left to report it.

Deliverable: skill at .agents/skills/workflow-ref-audit (run.sh + SKILL.md), plus a weekly canary workflow 'Workflow Reference Audit' at Monday 07:45 CT, deliberately placed before the Monday 09:00 pair so breakage is caught the same morning. The canary is a DETECTOR ONLY: its instruction forbids editing, archiving or disabling any workflow. Repairs go through Leon or an explicit GO.

Inventory discovery method: deployed functions cannot be listed from the sandbox, so the audit obtains the list by calling a function name that does not exist and reading the platform's 'Available: ...' error. Fully read-only.

First run: 61 files, 108 functions, 62 entities, 42 active. ZERO dead function references, zero dead entity references, zero never-fires among active workflows. The four STALE_ONE_TIME findings are inert leftovers already archived or inactive (see test_plan). One live CO-LOCATION (not a conflict): CAGE WATCH Sync Sentinel and Daily Bill Pay both at 08:00, unrelated systems, left alone deliberately.

Also fixed in the tool: collision counting now uses the registry's active list, because files persist for archived workflows and every archived schedule otherwise reads as a live collision. Seven false 'malformed workflow' findings were also eliminated by replacing a regex comment stripper that ate https:// in string values with a character scanner.
records.impact_assessment: Read-only. No workflow was edited, archived or disabled. No entity records modified by the audit itself. One new workflow added (the weekly canary), which costs one agent turn per week. The four stale one-time schedules are inert: three are already archived, and BLIND-3 is registered inactive.
records.implementation_plan: Character-scanner comment stripper (regex destroys URL schemes inside strings); checks DEAD_FUNCTION, DEAD_ENTITY, NEVER_FIRES, EMPTY_DEFINITION, STALE_ONE_TIME, COLLISION, BAD_TRANSITION, BAD_TASK, UNPARSEABLE; refuses to run on an inventory older than 7 days without --force because a stale inventory manufactures false DEAD_FUNCTION findings. Exit 1 only on findings that cause silent failure.
records.reason: Leon: 'yes we need that... this should be easy to do and fix this Collaps si the one thing we cannot have'
records.rollback_plan: Skill is inert unless run. Remove the weekly canary with manage_workflow(workflow_name='Workflow Reference Audit', action='archive'). No other state depends on it.
records.test_plan: Ran the audit against the live app: 61 files parsed, 0 unparseable, 108-function inventory seeded from a read-only probe, 62 entity names, 0 blocking findings. Verified the new workflow file on disk: cron '45 7 * * 1', timezone America/Chicago, single task run_audit with then=end. Verified the exclusion logic: collision count dropped from 5 groups to 1 after scoping to the active registry, and confirmed each of the 4 remaining stale one-time findings is inert (FL-1, Horsemen 7-Day Cycle Report and Horsemen Benchmark Kickoff are already archived; BLIND-3 is registered inactive).
records.title: CHG-20261030-04 — Workflow reference audit: the silent-failure detector

records.description:
CHG-20261030-03. Leon asked to 'merge everything' to stop the system collapsing. Finding: there are NO duplicate workflows. All 41 active workflows do distinct work, so merging them would have destroyed capability, which is the collapse risk he named. The real defect was schedule collision: three nightly jobs all fired at 03:00 CT, one of which MUTATES the fleet (jasperRemediation: resolves anomalies, rebalances agents, purges orphans) while the other two were measuring it (exportHubSnapshot digests, jasperCrossAppMonitor sweep). A remediation running concurrently with a snapshot can publish a health rollup of a fleet state that no longer exists, the same defect class as the stale 96.43 echo.

Change, ordered observe -> assess -> remediate: Nightly Hub Snapshot unchanged at 03:00; Daily Ecosystem Sweep 0 3 -> 20 3; Squirrel OS Daily Sweep 0 3 -> 40 3. Both re-saved with definitions byte-identically from disk, only the cron edited. Task lists unchanged: sweep+generate_manifest, and run_sweep+collect_metrics+report_to_operator. Nothing archived, deleted or disabled. Reversible with a single trigger edit.

Verification: re-parsed all 60 workflow files after the saves, 60 parsed / 0 failed. The 03:xx window now holds :00, :20, :40 with no two sharing a minute. Most other apparent collisions involve archived workflows and do not fire; the single remaining live pair (CAGE WATCH Sync Sentinel + Daily Bill Pay, both 08:00) touches unrelated systems and was deliberately left alone.

Not touched, and why: Nightly Hub Snapshot vs Nightly Entity Snapshot look redundant and are not (digest receipts vs actual export artifact, a deliberate belt-and-braces DR pair). Documented candidate merges that would be WRONG were also named so they are not done later as 'cleanup'. Receipt: WORKFLOW_CONSOLIDATION_2026-10-30.md.
records.impact_assessment: Nightly work is now serialized instead of overlapping: no capability removed, no workflow disabled, no alert path touched. Refresh cadence for every job is unchanged except the two moved by 20 and 40 minutes. The remediation job now runs against a fleet state that the snapshot and sweep have already finished reading.
records.implementation_plan: Read and parse all 60 workflow definition files with a comment stripper that preserves // inside string literals and URL schemes; a naive stripper produced seven false malformed-file findings on the first pass, corrected before judging any file. Group by cron_expression, then compare collision groups by the functions each job calls rather than by name. Re-save only the two jobs that needed moving, passing the definition object exactly as parsed so nothing but the trigger changed.
records.reason: Leon: 'we need to merge everying. i dot want this system collapsing. lets make very safe, very smart surgical fixes so that my systetm stengthends from this and not crater. i have put to much into this for that to happen.'
records.rollback_plan: Per workflow, restore the original cron: Daily Ecosystem Sweep -> 0 3 * * *, Squirrel OS Daily Sweep -> 0 3 * * *. Each is a single create_or_update_workflow save with change_summary 'rollback to 03:00'. Original definitions are preserved in /app/base44/workflows and in the receipt. No data was written, no records modified, no workflow archived, so no state restoration is required beyond the two triggers.
records.test_plan: Post-save audit script re-parsed all 60 files and re-grouped by cron: 60 parsed / 0 failures, 03:xx shows 03:00 Nightly Hub Snapshot, 03:20 Daily Ecosystem Sweep, 03:40 Squirrel OS Daily Sweep. Task-key lists read back from disk match the originals exactly. Both saves returned a new version hash.
records.title: CHG-20261030-03 — Nightly collision resolved: observe / assess / remediate staggered

records.description:
CHG-20261030-02. Two repairs: (1) SIM-B ops ticket queue drained from 6 open to 1 open, every closure carrying a resolution note that states no remediation was performed; (2) fleet telemetry blackout root-caused by direct probe and the measurement rule amended so autonomous telemetry and runtime reachability are reported as two fields and never merged.

TICKETS. Queue had 6 unresolved of 9, oldest 36 days, two of them P2. Nothing ever closed a ticket: a generator writes them and no dispatcher routes or drains them. Dispositioned via the app's own functions: MW-TKT-0002, 0004, 0005, 0008 resolved with notes; MW-TKT-0003 closed (note backfilled, because bulkCloseServiceTickets persists neither notes nor resolved_at); MW-TKT-0007 left OPEN as the one live ticket.

TELEMETRY. Conquest autonomousHeartbeat returns heartbeat_complete with 7 of 10 sub-tasks failing HTTP 403 and writes no SystemHeartbeat row. Runtimes are alive: War/Famine healthCheck green on db/entities/agents/auth at 14:15Z; Hypervisor wrote and resolved tickets minutes earlier. App-side fix required.

No PHI. Simulated Mirror Co. tenant only. Prototype disclaimer applies.
records.impact_assessment: Tickets: demo queue now shows a working desk (1 live ticket) instead of a 36-day backlog. No remediation is claimed for any closed ticket. Telemetry: number interpretation changes, and only by ADDING a field; the heartbeat ladder itself was not loosened, so the fleet still reads TELEMETRY_BLIND.
records.implementation_plan: Tickets: resolveServiceTicket(ticket_id, status, resolution_notes) per ticket, read back to verify status, resolved_at and notes. Rejected generateSyntheticTelemetry as a way to satisfy a liveness metric and rejected bulkCloseServiceTickets for anything needing a reason. Telemetry: probe each app's own deployed functions, record findings, amend .agents/rules/fleet-liveness-scoring.md with the two-measurement doctrine and the corrected 48h watchdog reading.
records.reason: Leon: 'lets fix all these issues this morning. Go on fixing telemety adn well start there. what is going on whti tickets fix that as well'
records.rollback_plan: Tickets: each closure is reversible by setting status back via resolveServiceTicket; original statuses are recorded (0002 in_progress, 0003 open, 0004 open, 0005 in_progress, 0008 open). Rule: amendment is append-only and a later dated amendment supersedes it, never deletes it.
records.test_plan: Post-write verification: simbListOpsTickets read back showing 8 closed/resolved, 1 open; per-ticket read-back of MW-TKT-0002 confirmed resolved_at plus note text landed; each resolution call returned success:true for the named ticket_id.
records.title: CHG-20261030-02 — Ticket queue dispositioned + fleet telemetry blackout root-caused

records.description: Two live enforcement changes and three read/record instruments. (1) ccrpPreWriteGate and ccrtRouteGate: position comparison restored (loop bound 1 -> 0); both redeployed. (2) New snapshotDrift (read-only snapshot comparison) and recordRestoreDrill (id-scoped, evidence-required drill stamp). (3) DR-2 cold restore drill executed and recorded against the hub BackupStatus row. (4) GATE-CERT v1.0 issued, offline and live.
records.implementation_plan: Patch loop bound in both gate sources; redeploy each; verify offline against the frozen corpus (10/10 refused, control accepted, previously-refused reasons unchanged); verify the deployed functions over HTTP on N06/N01/control; then run DR-2 and issue the certificate.
records.reason: Offline re-run of the CCR-N negative battery after 18.5 days of no gate activity found N06 (duplicate position) accepted by both deployed gates. The TypeScript port had replaced the Python reference's whole-dict comparison with a per-key loop bounded at 1, exempting KEYS[0]=position.
records.rollback_plan: Revert both gates to the deployed pre-change source, which differs by exactly one character per file (loop bound 1). Restoring the previous behaviour restores the defect, so rollback is only appropriate if the patch itself causes a false refusal; the control case is the check for that. Backups: /tmp/pre.ts.bak and /tmp/route.ts.bak were taken before the edit.
records.test_plan: GATE-CERT v1.0: corpus bytes 10/10 verified, instrument parity true, negatives refused 10/10, refusal layers 10/10 match, control accepted with 12 decisions, deployed gate 11/11 agreement. DR-2: archive hashes match receipt, 42 entities identical, 17 moved and all 17 attributed. No regression observed; fleet telemetry remains TELEMETRY_BLIND at 9.4, unrelated to this change.
